How is Arkansas organized when you sell a house here?

Arkansas has 75 counties, and nearly everything that touches a home sale runs through the county where the house sits. Pulaski County is the largest, with 404,611 residents in the figures Wikipedia cites from the Census Bureau, and Calhoun County is the smallest at 4,632. Ten counties have two county seats, which matters if you are hunting for the right courthouse. Arkansas County, for example, lists both Stuttgart and DeWitt, and Sebastian County lists Fort Smith and Greenwood.

The state map splits into very different selling environments. Benton and Washington counties in the northwest are the second and third most populous counties on the list, while Pulaski anchors the middle of the state with Little Rock, North Little Rock, Jacksonville and Sherwood. Smaller markets such as Paragould in Greene County or Texarkana in Miller County follow their own county rules and their own pace.

Below on this page you will find every county we cover, with the city pages and property tax guides we have written for each. Start with the county guide if you owe back taxes, and use the city page if you want local cost and timing detail. You can also browse our Arkansas guides by city and county for probate, foreclosure and tax topics.

Who handles property taxes on an Arkansas house?

Your county does, even though the state sets the framework. The Arkansas Assessment Coordination Division at the Department of Finance and Administration supervises assessment in all 75 counties, but the Division itself says taxes are assessed, administered, collected and distributed locally by each county.

The calendar runs over two years. The first year sets assessed values and millage rates, and the second year is when the money is collected. Because each assessment year is also the collection year for the year before, a seller can be dealing with two cycles at once.

The Division lists these dates for homeowners:

  • May 31: deadline to assess personal property and business personal property.
  • Third Monday in August: deadline to file an appeal with the county Board of Equalization.
  • October 15: deadline to pay property taxes.
  • October 15: deadline to file the Homestead Credit Application.

Who do you call? The county assessor answers value and homestead credit questions, and the county collector or treasurer office answers questions about what is owed. Our Arkansas property tax guide walks through the calendar, and each county guide below names the local offices. If a tax bill is unpaid at closing, ask the title company to pull the payoff before you agree to a closing date.

What does a sale cost in state transfer tax?

The real property transfer tax is $3.30 for every $1,000 of actual consideration on transactions above $100, according to the Department of Finance and Administration. It is charged on each deed or writing that conveys land or other realty, and it also applies to transfers of mineral rights.

A quick way to size it: a house that sells for $200,000 carries 200 units of $1,000, so the stamp tax on that price works out to $660. Who pays it is something the contract settles, and customs differ by deal. The state's Miscellaneous Tax Section handles stamps and corrections. Its Little Rock office can be reached at 501-682-7187 if a stamp shows the wrong figures.

How does foreclosure work in Arkansas?

Arkansas lenders may foreclose by court action or outside of court, and Nolo reports that most residential foreclosures in the state are nonjudicial because that route is quicker and cheaper. If you are behind on payments, the dates below decide how much room you have.

  • Federal rules usually bar a servicer from starting a foreclosure until you are more than 120 days past due.
  • The lender mails a pre-foreclosure notice at least ten days before starting.
  • A notice of default and intent to sell is recorded at least 60 days before the sale, with a copy mailed to you within 30 days after recording.
  • Notice also runs in a newspaper for four consecutive weeks before the sale.
  • The sale takes place on a weekday between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., at the property or the front door of the county courthouse.

You can reinstate the loan or pay it off before the sale. After a nonjudicial sale, Arkansas gives no redemption period. The buyer gets a deed within ten days and is entitled to immediate possession. A lender can also sue for a deficiency within 12 months after the sale, so the loss does not always end on the courthouse steps.

Selling before the sale date can stop the process and protect any equity. A cash sale as-is can fit that timeline because there is no buyer loan to wait on. If you are weighing this, read the guide to tax deed and tax lien sales too, since unpaid property tax follows its own clock.

What happens when you inherit a house in Arkansas?

Many inherited houses need a court filing before they can be sold, but small estates can skip the full process. Under Ark. Code 28-41-101, a distributee may collect and distribute estate assets without a personal representative when all of these are true:

  • No petition for a personal representative is pending or granted.
  • Forty-five days have passed since the death.
  • Property owned at death, less encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000. The homestead and statutory allowances for a spouse or minor children are left out of that count.
  • A distributee files an affidavit with the probate clerk of the circuit court in the proper county.

The clerk charges $25 to file the affidavit and $5 for each certified copy. If the estate includes real property, notice must be published within 30 days after filing, and creditors get three months from first publication to present claims. Larger estates go through formal probate in circuit court. Our Arkansas probate guide explains venue and who may serve, and the transfer on death deed guide covers houses that already name a beneficiary.

The state estate tax is covered in our estate and inheritance tax guide. Heirs often sell fast because carrying costs on a vacant house add up while paperwork moves.

Can you sell an Arkansas house with tenants in it?

Yes, but the lease and the notice rules shape the timeline. Arkansas defines unlawful detainer in Ark. Code 18-60-304. One ground is failing to pay rent when due and refusing to leave after three days' written notice to quit. Others include holding over after a lease ends and refusing a written demand to leave.

A buyer who purchases as-is can take the house with a tenant in place, and some sellers prefer that to a lengthy eviction. If you plan to deliver the house empty, read our eviction process guide and the notice rules page before sending anything. For rights on the tenant side, see landlord tenant law.

What does selling for cash as-is mean in Arkansas?

It means the buyer takes the house in its current condition, so you skip repairs, showings and loan approvals. We buy directly or bring a vetted cash buyer, and we ask you to confirm the facts about the house with the county office before closing.

The steps run in a short order:

  • You share the address, condition and any liens or back taxes.
  • We review the house and tell you what we can do.
  • A title company confirms ownership, pays off liens and handles the deed.
  • You close on a date that fits your situation.

Before you commit, gather the deed, the latest tax statement, and any mortgage payoff figure. For homesteads, the deadline to file the Homestead Credit Application is October 15, and your county assessor can say what credit applies. A buyer cannot claim a seller's prior age 65 or disabled freeze, so ask the assessor how a sale affects the bill. The Arkansas homestead guide lays this out. Questions about a deed? See the quitclaim deed guide.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Arkansas have?

Arkansas has 75 counties. Property taxes, deed recording and probate all run through the county where the house is located, so start with that county's offices.

Is foreclosure in Arkansas judicial?

It can be either. Lenders may go to court or use the out-of-court process, and most residential cases are nonjudicial. A notice of default must be recorded at least 60 days before the sale.

Is there a redemption period after a foreclosure sale?

Not after a nonjudicial sale. You can reinstate or pay off the loan before the sale, but Arkansas law gives no redemption period afterward.

How much is the Arkansas transfer tax?

The Department of Finance and Administration lists $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on transactions above $100.

Can I sell an inherited house without probate?

Sometimes. A small estate under $100,000, not counting the homestead and allowances, can use a distributee affidavit after 45 days. Larger estates need probate.

When are Arkansas property taxes due?

October 15 is the deadline to pay, and also the deadline to file the Homestead Credit Application. Appeals to the Board of Equalization are due the third Monday in August.

Can I sell a house that has tenants?

Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is with tenants in place. If you want the house empty, unpaid rent starts with three days of written notice to quit.
